To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a group of Gly‐ir/glycine transporter 2‐expressing neurons in the embryonal brain and spinal cord of zebrafish and that these neurons are highly stereotyped.

we have identified initially appearing glycinergic neurons in the zebrafish embryo and have shown their development and distribution in the hindbrain, spinal cord, and anterior brain, including the placodes.
the first Gly‐ir cells appeared in rhombomeric segments in the embryonic hindbrain and rostrally in the spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and function of glycinergic neurons in zebrafishes.

the initial development and the distribution of glycine immunoreactive (GIR) cells, and with their relationship to the expression of the glycine transporter 1 (glyt1) and the glycine transporter2 (glyt 2).
the development of glycine immunoreactive cells and fibers in the embryonic brain of the zebrafish, Danio rerio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Gly‐ir neurons are the first Gly‐ir neurons that appear in the zebrafish CNS, and they develop into Gly‐ir/glycine transporter 2 positive (Gly‐/glyt2‐positive), GABA‐negative, and glutamate‐negative neurons, and they are the first Gly neurons that are identified in the CNS of any vertebrates.

Gly‐ir cells are present at 20 hpf in the zebrafish hindbrain, and that they are highly stereotyped, with a one‐to‐one correspondence between Gly‐ir neurons and glyt2 mRNA‐expressing cells in the hindbrain.
Gly‐ir neurons are present in the embryonic hindbrain and spinal cord of zebrafish and that they are the precursors of glycinergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a pair of glycinergic neurons in the embryonically zebrafish hindbrain, which is a first report for vertebrate.
we have shown the first Gly‐ir cells are in hindbrain and spinal cord, and they have a stereotyped location.
we identified initially appearing Gly‐ir neurons and fibers in the embryonic brain and spinal cord, and that they are glyt2‐positive and become MiD2cm or MiD3cm neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a stereotyped population of Gly‐ir/glyT2‐positive neurons in rhomb 6 and rhomb 5 in the hindbrain that can be used to study glycine‐mediated inhibition in vertebrate embryonic development.
we have identified a group of glycinergic neurons in the embryonically developing zebrafish that are stereotypical in their position and morphology.
we found a new set of glycinergic cells that were previously unknown in vertebrate embryos.
